summary:
This bill is called the "Communities of Recovery Reauthorization Act of 2025." It changes a law called the Public Health Service Act. The law gives money, called grants, to help build communities of recovery.

Right now, the law says the government can spend $5 million each year for this from 2019 through 2023. This bill changes that amount. If this bill becomes a law, the government will be able to spend $17 million each year for five years, from 2026 through 2030.

A "fiscal year" is the way the government counts its spending year, which starts in October and ends in September. A "grant" is money the government gives to groups to help them do good work.

So, the main thing this bill does is give more money—$17 million a year instead of $5 million—to help build communities of recovery for the years 2026 to 2030.
